candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — hygiene and oral care
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the role of mechanical oral hygiene in reducing dental plaque and oral bacterial burden during hospitalization.

options.A: Toothbrushing mechanically removes dental plaque that can harbor pathogenic bacteria.
options.B: Toothbrushing replaces the need for suctioning or other airway-care measures.
options.C: Toothbrushing is performed only for appearance and has no health role.
options.D: Toothbrushing should be avoided because it increases hospital-acquired pneumonia risk.

candidate.rationale: CDC notes that dental plaque begins to reform within hours after toothbrushing and grows rapidly if not mechanically removed. Plaque can harbor pathogenic bacteria that may contribute to hospital-acquired pneumonia if aspirated. Oral care remains relevant even when a patient is not eating orally. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Dental plaque reforms rapidly and can contain pathogenic bacteria; regular toothbrushing mechanically removes plaque and is part of hospital oral-care practice.
candidate.source_document_title: Oral Health in Healthcare Settings to Prevent Pneumonia Toolkit
candidate.source_locator: Background — dental plaque formation, pathogenic bacteria, aspiration; Sample Oral Care Procedures
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: Why is regular toothbrushing clinically relevant for a hospitalized client even when the client is not eating by mouth?
